source.title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density

accepted.question_text: At present collider energies, for QCD processes involving partons with small longitudinal momentum fraction x and transverse momentum kT of order the saturation scale Qs(x), is the nonlinear parton-saturation description implemented by the Color Glass Condensate phenomenology actually necessary, or can the data be described adequately by purely linear gluon distributions supplemented with a non-perturbative ad hoc cutoff? Here parton saturation means the weakly coupled nonlinear QCD regime that appears when parton densities grow at small x, and Qs(x) is the momentum scale separating dense and dilute regimes.

evidence.quote: The emergence of this non-linear regime, called parton saturation, in which QCD stays weakly coupled, is a fundamental consequence of QCD dynamics.
the separation between the dense and dilute regimes is characterized by a momentum scale Qs(x), called the saturation scale, which increases as x decreases.

2.1. A big open question: is parton saturation relevant at today’s collider? In other words, can one get away with using a purely-linear gluon distribution with a necessary non-perturbative ad hoc cutoff, or do we need to properly take into account dynamics at kT ∼ Qs, as suggested in Fig. 1 ? On top of being much more satisfactory from the theoretical point-of-view, is the latter solution necessary ?

accepted.question_text: How fast, and by what QCD dynamics, does a high-energy nuclear collision observable transition from the nonlinear saturation regime to the high-transverse-momentum leading-twist regime, given that current running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov small-x evolution equations do not include the DGLAP limit and predict that proton-nucleus nuclear-modification observables return to unity only at unrealistically large transverse momentum pT?

evidence.quote: How fast is the transition from the saturation regime to the high-pT (leading-twist) regime ? The most up-to-date non-linear QCD evolution equations, such as the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) equation, do not contain the DGLAP limit, hence after some evolution down in x (reflected in the data at forward rapidities), RpA predictions reach unity only at unrealistically large values of pT . This is an open question, to which p+A collisions at the LHC should have already provided some answers, once electron-nucleus (e+A) data become available.

accepted.question_text: What is the transverse impact-parameter dependence of the nuclear gluon density and of the saturation scale Qs in a nucleus, and is the current phenomenological Color Glass Condensate practice of modeling a nucleus as Woods-Saxon distributed CGCs whose gluon densities are evolved independently at different impact parameters sufficient for a conceptually accurate description of small-x nuclear structure?

evidence.quote: What is the impact parameter dependence of the nuclear gluon density and saturation scale? This has always been the main non-perturbative input in CGC calculations.

What is done in the most advanced CGC phenomenological studies, is to treat the nucleus as a collection of Woods-Saxon distributed CGCs, and to evolve (down in x) the resulting gluon density at different impact parameters independently. But is this good enough ? Even though in order to describe p+A collision data it seems it is, conceptually it is not good enough, and e+A collisions are crucial to answer this question by precisely imaging the transverse structure of nuclei at small-x.

accepted.question_text: How does QCD make the transition from the high-parton-density saturation regime, where small-x gluons form a weakly coupled nonlinear many-body system, to the confinement regime of QCD?

evidence.quote: The emergence of this non-linear regime, called parton saturation, in which QCD stays weakly coupled, is a fundamental consequence of QCD dynamics.

There are more fundamental questions, still unexplored, in the field of QCD at high parton density. How does the transition from the saturation regime to confinement happen? Does the QCD coupling run with Qs? Are classical fields still the right degrees of freedom? What are the universality properties of the saturation regime? p+A and e+A collisions offer special opportunities to explore this many-body system of strongly-correlated gluons.

accepted.question_text: If nonlinear running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution successfully predicts nuclear-to-proton structure-function ratios in inclusive electron-nucleus deep inelastic scattering, can the linear EPS09 nuclear parton-distribution approach simultaneously accommodate both F2 and FL electron-nucleus data when saturation sets in according to the rcBK prediction, or would failure to do so make the rcBK-based description uniquely favored? Here F2 and FL are the two structure functions whose linear combination gives the total virtual-photon–nucleus cross section and which provide access to integrated quark and gluon distributions, respectively.
accepted.context_brief: Linear versus nonlinear description of inclusive e+A DIS

evidence.quote: Inclusive DIS is pictured in Fig. 4 (left). This process consists in measuring the total γ∗+A cross section, a linear combination of two observables: the F2 and FL structure functions. These provide access to the integrated (with respect to the transverse dynamics) distributions of quarks and gluons respectively.

The approach based on non-linear small-x evolution (rcBK [12]) is predictive, and therefore would undergo a stringent test. If successful, then a further question can be asked: can the linear EPS09 approach [13] (whose errors will be reduced by p+A constraints once LHC data are available) simultaneously accommodate F2 and FL e+A data, if saturation sets in according to the rcBK prediction? If not, then the latter would provide the unique data description.

accepted.question_text: At a future Electron Ion Collider, can combined measurements of the F2 and FL structure functions in inclusive electron-nucleus deep inelastic scattering discriminate between linear and nonlinear QCD evolution, as combined F2 and FL measurements are expected to do at the Large Hadron electron Collider?
accepted.context_brief: EIC discriminating power of F2 and FL

evidence.quote: At the LHeC, the combined F2 and FL measurements have that potential to discriminate between linear and non-linear QCD evolution. At the EIC, studies are ongoing to determine whether that is also true. In any case, it is the combination of F2 and FL which makes the γ∗+A total cross section potentially a smoking-gun measurement. Precisely measuring FL is therefore crucial, and this requires an e+A collision energy scan.

accepted.question_text: In electron-nucleus diffractive vector-meson production or deeply virtual Compton scattering, can the incoherent diffractive background from nuclear breakup be removed efficiently enough to access the first minimum and maximum of the momentum-transfer distribution, thereby enabling extraction of transverse spatial distributions and correlations of partons from the t dependence of the cross section?

evidence.quote: Diffractive vector meson production (or deeply virtual Compton scattering when the produced vector particle is a photon) is pictured in Fig. 7 (left). This exclusive process provides access to the spatial distributions (and correlations) of partons in the transverse plane, unlike the more inclusive processes discussed before. Indeed, this information can be obtained through a Fourier transformation of the t dependence of the cross section, where t is the square of the momentum transferred by the target.

Coming back to the momentum transfer dependence, Fig. 8 shows diffractive J/Ψ and φ production off a gold nucleus. Depending on how efficiently the incoherent background can be removed (incoherent diffraction allows the possible break-up of the target nucleus into its constituent nucleons), one could access the first minimum and maximum of the distribution.
